denfertLandingRoom.observation: The Denfert axonometric section shows a turn from the visitor corridor through a walled approach room to the head of the spiral.
denfertLandingRoom.model: The model adds plaster partition walls and a framed doorway inside the fitted annex at the upper landing datum.
denfertLandingRoom.limitations: The Denfert stair approach uses a short enclosed room and open doorway, based on the architect’s cutaway. The door, shaft and partition positions within the footprint remain approximate.

placementTrial.maskBasis: Local landing pads inset 1 cm and clipped to the independent portal replacement footprints. Sub-0.1 square metre fragments are omitted.

scope: All four draft levels retain the two public portal placements and fit the former Fontis street front to its mapped footprint. Street and close-up show the route return and Fontis junction. The full public route and the passage beyond the Fontis upper landing remain provisional.

reneCotyGalleryReturn.planningSourceType: Public preview of a Paris Musées route planning attachment
reneCotyGalleryReturn.geometryBasis: The Paris Musées planning diagram marks the bends toward René-Coty and a separate guided branch toward the former Fontis exit. The revised draft follows the exit-side return and joins the Fontis gallery there. Registration uses both public portals and the Fontis address. Exact junction geometry and final as-built underground positions remain estimates.

controlTiepoints.name: Fontis former exit at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel

reneCotyGalleryReturn.limitation: The draft public centerline measures 775.2 m. The Paris Musées planning trace measures about 785 m when fitted to the two public portals and former Fontis address. The museum lists a 1.5 km visit. The difference remains unresolved.
